newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator Domenici gives budget talks one week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator Domenici gives budget talks one week.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici said Monday at the start of the week's balanced budget talks with the White House he was committed to giving the process one week before he seeks an alternative route to solving the budget problems.
"This is the week to do it," the New Mexico Republican said. "There are still a lot of major issues but we are willing to tackle them."

"I remain pretty committed to the proposition that we've got about a week, and after the week, if we don't get it done, I think we go another route, go without the President and try to put a bi-partisan budget together up here," he said as he entered the closed-door talks with White House Budget Director Frank Raines.
White House economic adviser Gene Sperling praised "the goodwill in the room" and said President Clinton remains committed to protecting childrens' health, education and the environment.
The Monday bargaining session was to discuss Medicaid health care for the poor and defense programs.

The negotiators also included Senator Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, the Budget committee's senior Democrat, House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, Republican of Ohio, Rep. John Spratt of South Carolina, the senior Democrat on the House Budget panel, and Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala.
